reasons: Lake identity is verified and lists case_name as Carroll v. United States, court as U.S. Supreme Court, and year as 1925.
Lake citations list official 267 U.S. 132, parallels 45 S. Ct. 280 and 69 L. Ed. 543, and vendor-neutral 1925 U.S. LEXIS 361.
Cached text header also shows 267 U.S. 132, 45 S.Ct. 280, 69 L.Ed. 543, and a 1925 decision date.
residual_risks: Lake identity date_decided is 1925-11-26 while cached text says Decided March 2, 1925; the reviewed assertion states only the year, so this did not defeat the citation/year assertion.

reasons: Lake treatment scope_note identifies Carroll as the origin of the automobile exception.
Opinion text states the true rule that a warrantless search and seizure of an automobile or other vehicle is valid on probable cause that it contains seizable contraband.
Opinion paragraph 37 supplies the vehicle-mobility distinction that anchors the automobile-exception home role.
residual_risks: The opinion itself does not use the modern phrase automobile exception; that label is supported by the lake scope_note.

defect.evidence_quote: On reason and authority the true rule is that if the search and seizure without a warrant are made upon probable cause, that is, upon a belief, reasonably arising out of circumstaces known to the seizing officer, that an automobile or other vehicle contains that which by law is subject to seizure and destruction, the search and seizure are valid.
defect.problem: The holding is supportable in substance but the field is truncated with an ellipsis and should state the contraband/illegal-merchandise and mobility/impracticability limits expressly.
defect.proposed_fix: Origin of the automobile exception: when officers have probable cause to believe an automobile or other vehicle contains contraband or illegal merchandise, they may search it without a warrant where securing a warrant is not practicable because the vehicle can be quickly moved.

reasons: Opinion paragraph 26 supports warrantless automobile/vehicle search and seizure on probable cause for items subject to seizure and destruction.
Opinion paragraph 37 supports the fixed-structure versus vehicle mobility rationale.
Lake scope_note supports the historical label Origin of the automobile exception.
residual_risks: Do not broaden the holding beyond contraband or illegal merchandise and the warrant-impracticability rationale supplied by Carroll.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Replace the open-ended ellipsis with the proposed complete holding.

reasons: Lake identity lists court as U.S. Supreme Court and court_level as scotus, supporting the SCOTUS authority-weight label.
